title: The Great Handwashing Rescue
goal: Help Elder Rowan wash away sticky Grumble Dust by scrubbing every part of your hands with soap and clean water for 20 full seconds.
steps: Talk to Elder Rowan by the Town Square fountain.
Wet hands, lather soap, and scrub all 5 hand zones for 20 seconds.
Rinse clean and dry to earn your first Hygiene Crystal fragment!
didYouKnow: Washing your hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds (about humming 'Happy Birthday' twice) lifts away germs from palms, fingers, thumbs, and under fingernails!
didYouKnowOlder: According to the CDC and WHO, soap molecules break apart the lipid membrane of many viruses and lift bacteria off your skin—making a full 20-second scrub one of the strongest everyday defenses against illness.
trustedAdultNote: If you ever feel unwell with a fever or stomach ache, remember to tell a trusted adult or doctor.

title: Brush Brigade
goal: Old Mr. Splash has a grumpy toothache! Put the healthy brushing steps in the right order to keep smiles bright.
steps: Visit Old Mr. Splash at the Bathhouse & Well.
Arrange the 5 tooth-brushing steps in the proper order.
Deliver fluoride toothpaste care and restore sparkle!
didYouKnow: Brushing your teeth twice a day for 2 minutes with a pea-sized drop of fluoride toothpaste helps sweep away plaque and keep enamel strong.
didYouKnowOlder: Plaque bacteria feed on sugars and produce acids that wear down tooth enamel; brushing gently for 2 minutes twice daily (plus flossing) neutralizes acid buildup and protects gums.
trustedAdultNote: If a tooth hurts or feels sensitive, ask a trusted adult to help you visit a dentist.

title: Clean Water Quest
goal: Inspect Sunnybrook's water sources with Old Mr. Splash and identify which water is safe to drink and which needs boiling or filtering.
steps: Check the Bathhouse & Well spring stations.
Sort safe treated/boiled water from unsafe stagnant or muddy sources.
Restore the Hygiene Wellness Crystal!
didYouKnow: Clear-looking water isn't always germ-free! Safe drinking water comes from covered, tested taps or water that has been properly filtered and boiled.
didYouKnowOlder: Even crystal-clear streams can carry microscopic parasites or bacteria. WHO guidelines recommend boiling, certified filtration, or safe municipal treatment before drinking unknown water.
trustedAdultNote: Always ask a trusted adult before drinking from outdoor streams or unfamiliar taps.

title: Rainbow Plate
goal: Help Baker Bea prepare a colorful, balanced festival meal with veggies, fruits, whole grains, protein, and water.
steps: Meet Baker Bea at Sunnybrook Market.
Fill all sections of the Rainbow Plate with balanced food groups.
Share the colorful feast with the village!
didYouKnow: Eating a 'rainbow' of colorful fruits and vegetables alongside whole grains and protein gives your body different vitamins, fiber, and steady energy to play!
didYouKnowOlder: Different plant pigments—like orange beta-carotene or purple anthocyanins—deliver distinct micronutrients. Pairing half a plate of produce with whole grains and lean proteins supports sustained focus and growth.
trustedAdultNote: Every body is unique—ask a trusted adult or doctor if you have food allergies or special nutrition needs.

title: Sugar Sneak
goal: Some packaged snacks at the Market hide lots of added sugar! Inspect the snack labels and pick the everyday balanced choices.
steps: Inspect snack labels with Baker Bea.
Spot drinks and bars with sneaky added sugars like high-fructose syrup.
Choose whole-food snacks that give steady energy without a sugar crash.
didYouKnow: Sweet treats are fine once in a while, but sugary sodas and candies can sneak in lots of added sugar without filling you up. Water and whole fruit give steady energy!
didYouKnowOlder: WHO guidelines suggest keeping free added sugars low—checking nutrition labels for words like 'syrup', 'sucrose', or 'dextrose' helps you spot hidden sugars in flavored drinks and snacks.
trustedAdultNote: Ask a trusted adult to read ingredient labels together next time you grocery shop.

title: Harvest Helper
goal: Farmer Fig's harvest baskets tumbled in the wind! Sort the fresh foods into Grains, Produce, Protein, and Dairy/Calcium baskets.
steps: Talk to Farmer Fig at the Market stalls.
Sort 10 harvest items into their proper food group baskets.
Restore the Nutrition Wellness Crystal!
didYouKnow: No single food has everything we need—combining grains for fuel, produce for vitamins, protein for muscles, and calcium foods for bones keeps your body strong!
didYouKnowOlder: Balanced meals combine complex carbohydrates, essential amino acids from varied proteins, healthy fats, and micronutrients like calcium and vitamin D for bone density during ages 8–14.
trustedAdultNote: A trusted adult or registered dietitian can help plan meals around your favorite family traditions.

title: Field Day Fitness
goal: Hit the Sports Field 2.5D track with Coach Kiko! Time your jumps and dashes to the rhythm to build heart-pumping stamina.
steps: Meet Coach Kiko at the Sports Field track.
Time your leaps and sprints across the obstacle rhythm track.
Feel your energy soar!
didYouKnow: Kids and teens thrive with about 60 minutes of fun movement a day—like running, biking, dancing, or playing tag—to strengthen the heart and lungs!
didYouKnowOlder: Both WHO and CDC recommend at least 60 minutes daily of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity for youth, combining aerobic endurance with bone- and muscle-strengthening play.
trustedAdultNote: If you ever feel dizzy or out of breath during sports, pause, drink water, and tell a coach or trusted adult.

title: Stretch It Out
goal: A villager woke up feeling stiff as a fencepost! Guide them through a safe warm-up sequence before vigorous play.
steps: Check in with Coach Kiko by the field benches.
Order the safe warm-up and gentle stretch sequence.
Earn the Flexibility Ribbon!
didYouKnow: Warming up gently with arm circles and light marching before sports wakes up your muscles and joints so you move safely and smoothly.
didYouKnowOlder: Dynamic warm-ups gradually raise heart rate and muscle temperature, improving joint range of motion and lowering strain risk before high-intensity movement.
trustedAdultNote: Stretching should feel gentle, never sharp or painful—stop and tell a trusted adult if anything hurts.

title: Walk the Trail
goal: Pace steady steps along the scenic Sunnybrook Trail, hydrating at water stops to reach the overlook and claim the Exercise Crystal!
steps: Begin the trail challenge with Coach Kiko.
Keep a steady walking cadence and sip water at rest stops.
Restore the Fitness Wellness Crystal!
didYouKnow: Even everyday walking adds up! Taking walking breaks, pacing yourself, and sipping water keeps your body energized without wearing out.
didYouKnowOlder: Steady aerobic movement like brisk walking boosts circulation, releases mood-lifting endorphins, and pairs naturally with regular hydration breaks.
trustedAdultNote: Always hike or walk new trails with a buddy or trusted adult.

title: Sleepy Sam
goal: Step inside Granny Luna's cutaway Cozy Cottage to build a calm, screen-free bedtime routine for sleepy Sam.
steps: Visit Granny Luna inside Cozy Cottage.
Arrange the calm wind-down routine in the best order for restful sleep.
Help Sam drift off peacefully!
didYouKnow: Kids ages 6–12 need about 9–12 hours of sleep (and teens 8–10 hours) each night! Turning off bright screens before bed helps your brain know it's time to rest.
didYouKnowOlder: Consistent bedtimes and screen-free wind-down routines allow melatonin levels to rise naturally, supporting memory consolidation, growth hormone release, and emotional resilience.
trustedAdultNote: If trouble sleeping lasts many nights, talk with a trusted adult or doctor.

title: Worry Clouds
goal: Grumble Fog has stirred up Worry Clouds! Follow Granny Luna's gentle 4-second breathing rhythm to calm the mind and claim the Rest Crystal.
steps: Sit by the Cozy Cottage hearth with Granny Luna.
Complete 3 calm belly-breathing cycles (Inhale · Hold · Exhale).
Restore the Rest Wellness Crystal!
didYouKnow: Taking slow belly breaths tells your nervous system that you're safe—helping worried thoughts float by like clouds in the sky.
didYouKnowOlder: Slow diaphragmatic breathing activates the parasympathetic nervous system, lowering heart rate and easing stress when school or life feels overwhelming.
trustedAdultNote: Talking about big feelings with a trusted adult, teacher, or counselor is always a brave and helpful step.

title: Germ Detectives
goal: Put on Teacher Tam's prototype Germ Goggles to inspect the School classroom and clean up hidden germ hotspots!
steps: Meet Teacher Tam at Sunnybrook School.
Toggle your Germ Goggles lens to spot glowing germ hotspots.
Wipe down shared surfaces and unlock the Germ Goggles tool!
didYouKnow: Germs love high-touch spots like doorknobs, shared pencils, and desks! Cleaning shared surfaces and washing hands stops germs from hitching a ride.
didYouKnowOlder: Fomites—frequently touched objects like handles, keyboards, and desks—transfer respiratory and stomach microbes. Routine surface hygiene plus handwashing breaks the chain of transmission.
trustedAdultNote: Ask a trusted adult before using household cleaning sprays or wipes.

title: Sneeze Safe
goal: Achoo! Practice friendly sneeze & cough etiquette with Teacher Tam so classrooms stay comfortable and safe for everyone.
steps: Join Teacher Tam's health lesson at the School.
Sequence the safe cough/sneeze etiquette & mask-care steps.
Help classmates stay healthy together!
didYouKnow: Coughing or sneezing into your elbow ('the vampire sneeze') or a tissue—and wearing a clean mask when sick—keeps tiny droplets from spreading to friends.
didYouKnowOlder: Respiratory droplets travel meters when uncovered; covering coughs with a bent elbow, disposing of tissues immediately, and washing hands dramatically reduces spread.
trustedAdultNote: If you have a cough or fever, stay home to rest and check in with a trusted adult or doctor.

title: Vaccine Visit
goal: Nurse Nora explains how vaccines train your body's friendly Immune Team! Guide the Immune Defenders in a calm practice drill.
steps: Visit Nurse Nora at Sunnybrook Clinic.
Match immune shield trainers to build memory protection without fear.
Earn the Shield Apprentice Badge!
didYouKnow: Vaccines are like a safe practice drill for your immune system—they teach your body to recognize a germ ahead of time so it can stay strong!
didYouKnowOlder: Vaccines introduce harmless antigens that train B-cells and T-cells to build immunological memory, enabling rapid, targeted defense before an illness can take hold.
trustedAdultNote: It's normal to have questions at a checkup—always ask a trusted adult or doctor what a vaccine protects against.

title: Mosquito Patrol
goal: Patrol around the Clinic courtyard with Nurse Nora to tip out standing water in flowerpots and buckets where mosquitoes breed.
steps: Meet Nurse Nora outside the Clinic.
Spot and empty all standing-water containers in the yard.
Restore the Prevention Wellness Crystal!
didYouKnow: Mosquitoes lay eggs in tiny puddles of still water! Tipping out buckets, birdbaths, and flowerpot saucers helps keep neighborhoods bite-free.
didYouKnowOlder: Standing water is the primary breeding habitat for vector mosquitoes. Eliminating stagnant containers weekly is a key CDC & WHO community prevention strategy.
trustedAdultNote: Ask a trusted adult about safe insect repellent or window screens if mosquitoes are around.

title: Clear the Grumble Fog
goal: All 5 Wellness Crystals shine! Ascend the Misty Forest steps to the Boss Arena and unite Hygiene, Nutrition, Fitness, Rest, and Prevention to lift the Grumble Fog!
steps: Collect all 5 Wellness Crystals from Sunnybrook's villagers.
Climb into the Misty Forest Boss Arena.
Use everything you learned to calm and clear the Grumble Fog!
didYouKnow: Wellness isn't just one big thing—it's small daily habits working together: clean hands, colorful foods, joyful movement, restful sleep, and looking out for one another!
didYouKnowOlder: Whole-person health integrates physical hygiene, balanced nutrition, daily movement, mental rest, and community prevention—habits that reinforce one another for lifelong resilience.
trustedAdultNote: Keep sharing what you learn with family, friends, and trusted adults!
